newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian paramilitaries free guerrilla's sister.
newsitem.headline: Colombian paramilitaries free guerrilla's sister.

text.p: Right-wing paramilitaries freed the sister of a leftist guerrilla leader on Monday almost five months after she was kidnapped in northwest Colombia, police said.

Janeth Torres, sister of Pablo Catatumbo, one of the National leaders of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), was seized on July 29 as part of a wave of retaliatory abductions by right-wing paramilitary gangs.

One of these groups, the so-called Peasant Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba (ACCU), is still holding at least three relatives of rebel leaders to force the FARC to stop kidnapping civilians to get ransoms to fill its war chests.

Last week, the government offered a $1 million bounty for Carlos Castano, the feared leader of the ACCU. His gang has been blamed for more almost 100 killings across northern Colombia in the last month.
